question: When a protected combat reaches a winning selection, does the result consumer keep the original winning unit alive and mark the original loser dead, and what returned winner casualty limits hold for any figure count?

scope.qualification: Static claims about selected native code and supplied engine memory profiles. They do not run the game, do not show that the supplied memory is reached by a legal player action and do not prove arbitrary multi figure retry termination, all natural battle admissions, all callback effects, network delivery, display and internal strength equality, or survival in later combat.

definitions.winningSelection: The attacker's combat figure mask is nonempty and the defender's is empty, or the reverse for a defender win.
definitions.appliedVictory: The matching result marks the original opposing unit dead while the original winning unit stays alive.
definitions.originalUnitSurvival: The same occupied unit record, owner and type remain with the dead bit clear at the stated consumer return. It does not mean unchanged rank, no wounds or survival in later battles.
definitions.protectionCap: A protection flag asks for retries of losing selections. The shared cap 1000 alone does not prove a winning result. The Catapult kernel proves a win before the cap for every starting state.

sufficientCondition.K: The fixed source and kernel conditions of a proved selection case: the actual one sided protection and override, definition masks, army bytes, history, casualties, positive safe strengths and sampled generator inputs. The preserved modulus is 4294954991 and the scale bits are 0x3DF0000301109066. All 4294967296 starting state words and any draw counter word are covered by the Catapult certificate. File initial values alone do not prove those current samples.
sufficientCondition.L: The same final masks and participant generations through human writeback, the actual matching local result record reaching the consumer, the Catapult definition flag paths, valid disjoint memory and normal finite helper completion with concrete noninterference conditions. Normal ABI return alone does not establish a helper's memory effects.
implication: => the same battle's casualty payload is applied to the original participants
=> original attacker alive and original defender dead at consumer return
sufficientCondition.qualification: A rounded battle screen ratio is not enough to choose a row. The current internal operands and the full row conditions must match. The strict local profile instantiates L for its supplied values. General world L contracts stay necessary where the extensions do not discharge them.

returnedWinnerCasualtyInvariant.domain: Every positive definition mask B contained in bits 0 through 2, including prior casualty subsets, under the selected payload path.
returnedWinnerCasualtyInvariant.figures: n is the number of supported base figure slots. The full figure mask of an ordinary unit is B. For an army it is E = B | (B << 3) | (B << 6).
returnedWinnerCasualtyInvariant.selection: The attempted selection starts from the supported slots without prior wounds, expanded the same way for an army. Both participants must start nonempty. Each exchange removes exactly one set figure bit. An attempt stops when one side empties, with at most 17 removals for two nine figure armies. The 18 entry side and ordinal arrays keep a final sentinel in their 144 byte frame extent.
returnedWinnerCasualtyInvariant.cardinalityRetry: After the capped rejection checks, 0x82CDC7F8..0x82CDC87C retries a sole army winner whose remaining mask has at most one set bit. These retries have no protection counter cap, so every returned army winner has at least two raw surviving figures. Eventual termination for every army fight is not proved.
formulas: rawLosses = 3*n - r for an army winner with r remaining raw figures
returnedWinnerCasualtyInvariant.consequence: An ordinary winner has a nonempty remaining mask, so its casualties cannot equal its full definition mask. The consumer rebuilds that many supported base bits in order 2, 1, 0, so it cannot rebuild the full definition mask for a returned winner and the later definition equality defeat test is false. This proves the selected casualty conversion safe. Lifetime and result transport remain subject to L.

warriorArcher.types: Warrior (UnitType 6) and Archer (UnitType 9) both have definition mask 7, three supported base slots. A healthy army expands to 0x1FF, nine raw combat figure slots. These are developer quantities, not separate surviving unit records or displayed health pips.

rows.treatment: can pass; at least one base slot remains
retried before a final result is returned

warriorArcher.examples: Remaining mask 3 gives raw 0x1FC and rebuilt base casualties 6, leaving base bit 0. Remaining mask 1 and raw 0x1FE would rebuild casualties 7, and the final retry excludes it. The one base slot Catapult Army counterexample is also excluded: full 0x49 with remaining 1 and raw 0x48 would convert to full base casualty 1, but retries.

humanResult.source: The Catapult source (UnitType 16, flags 0x00200028) bypasses defender retirement at 0x82CDCD7C and attacker retirement and replacement at 0x82CDD120 and 0x82CDD164. The former needs definition flags & 0x1 nonzero, the latter low byte flags & 0x81 nonzero. The Catapult excludes both. Its final mask meanings also survive the separately proved local assignment bypasses. Nonvolatile register preservation alone would not establish them.
humanResult.writeback: On the human route frame 148 = 1, actual local player equality and post presentation global 0x8312B8C8 = -1 select the writeback of the preserved final mask. Ordinary masks 1 and 0 give raw casualties 0 and 1, packed as 0x01001000. For the healthy Army winner full mask 0x49 XOR remaining 0x49 also gives 0 and the defender mask 0 gives raw 1. Its consumer army conversion computes floor((0 + 1)/3) = 0. The result command carries no defender player identity sufficient to replace the consumer's normalization.
humanResult.identities: Let A and D be distinct opposed records in the player bank at 0x830F2BF0 + 84*(256*player + slot), slots 0 through 255. The occupied live original participants are captured before cleanup. 0x82CD7A60 keeps the original actor player and slot separately from the target player and slot. 0x82CFE450 performs a fresh live record scan at the destination and its actual output must still name D. Catapult flag 0x10000 is clear, so the later candidate replacement loop is bypassed. A live record at the same slot number after reallocation would not establish the original identity.

delivery.bridge: The local command 42 bridge needs the actual full append and drain cursor lineage, at most 32 occupied ring slots, no overwrite, reset or load, the matching five word copy, busy bit 0x4000 clear and actual completed dispatch. Submitting the record or returning from the resolver establishes none of these. The network receive path is outside this local contract.
delivery.returnCodes: The narrow consumer path returns 0 through 0x82CD9968. At 0x82CDFAEC and 0x82CDFAF0 that value branches to 0x82CE16AC, where 0x82CE16B0 sets dispatcher return 1. A completed consumer 0 therefore consumes the matching queue record successfully. Busy refusal at 0x82CDFAC8 is a separate dispatcher 0 before the consumer runs. The consumer's return value must not replace the handler's queue consumption result. The survivor endpoint precedes later dispatcher movement or another command.

sameRecord.preconditions: At submission: network byte 0x8314F10B = 0, preliminary polling bit 0x400 clear in 0x830E4550, actor busy bit 0x4000 clear, and initial full queue cursors W = R = q with 0 <= q < 0x40000000. sameRecord.diagnostics: 0x82CD4CF0 has only save and restore writes. The type 42 arm of 0x82CD5400 is a pure string address return. 0x822DF8A0 is a no store zero return leaf. requiredHelperMemoryConditions.preserve: For worlds outside the proved profiles, other transitive effects of the full sets of helper paths below stay explicit conditions. They must preserve original participant generations and backing, owner and type bytes, the actor dead bit 31 and defender dead bit 31 after retirement. They must not retire or reallocate either original record, replace the world or alias their outputs into protected gameplay storage. They must preserve the active frame's original actor homes 804 and 812, target homes 112 and 124, address carriers and routing inputs through their last uses. Frame 136 is needed only through its last defeat and loser tail decision. Frames 152, 164 and 820 are needed through their later routing reads. Intended normalizer, query and presentation outputs are allowed in their documented homes. Each save and restore frame needs valid distinct storage. These are memory write contracts. Ordinary ABI return does not prove noninterference.

The strict profile has bit 0x80 clear in every reached live unit's tile halfword and all 128 city owner bytes 0xFF. The unit child bypass is (tile & 0x4080) != 0x80, which excludes 0x82D030D0. currentEvidence.method: Read-only memory word queries of the selected native spans compared with the supported flat image, supplied state interpreters over the selected instruction words with semantic mutation controls, and narrow generated code corroboration.
deliverySpans: the dispatch prelude and type 42 arm
verification: Integer word replays passed 52 mask constructions, 1508 two sided casualty and defeat cases, 704 allowed survivor masks, 8192 final cardinality and counter cases, 1344 shared counter and history cases and 4608 selected bit removals. Two 17 removal sequences checked the array sentinels. The forced selection checks add 20 source cases, 12 selection cases and four source to load compositions. Twenty semantic instruction mutants were rejected.

Consumer checks passed 25 groups and 14 semantic mutations plus 571 native branch and call target comparisons with zero generated mismatch. The consumer inventory has 329 branch class words, 86 calls and 114 stores. The control flow graphs for ordinary and Army units cover 1094 and 1110 words, the same 43 possible call sites and 73 and 74 stores. The one added Army store clears actor casualties at 0x82CD7CEC. The raw ordinary and Army fixtures execute 4612 and 4718 instruction steps with 12 calls and 46 and 47 stores. They run the native normalizer and UnitKill.

Helper checks passed 81 groups, 32 supplied mode mask cases and ten mutations. Whole recount checks passed 22 groups across the three profiles, executing 84844, 84954 and 86233 instructions and 23851, 23852 and 23875 stores, each with 44 calls and the same normalized defender.

Local transport checks passed eight cursor and classifier cases and 19 mutations, including actual human actor 0, nonhuman controls, q = 0, 31, 32 and 0x3FFFFFFF, busy rollback and consumer 0 against dispatcher 1.

Callback checks passed nine native cases across 258 executed words, 27 identity pins and 20 mutations. The registered [E,0,0] notification executes 214 interpreted instructions, 9 calls and 37 stores. Preparation executes 188, 7 and 22 for each original participant.

Populated checks passed 64 checks, 18 typed entry runs across the six whole consumer profiles, eight changed source controls and seven rejected invalid source guards. All native and composed reads and writes exclude the eight generator state and counter bytes.

Presentation checks passed 26 groups and 13 mutations, including 594 independently decoded branch and memory operand comparisons and 17 local execution cases. The combined supplied state execution reaches 0x82CD9C08 in 7550 instructions, 24 calls and 147 stores. It is not a continuous replay from 0x82CD9C08 through the kernel and presentation to the emitter.

A mask 0 direct 0x82D11AD8 control executes the native map subtree 0x821B8CD0, 0x821CDE20 and 0x827F18C8 three times and returns through 0x82D13518 in 98600 instructions. It is not composed with the mask 1 result. A whole consumer mask 0 control stops earlier at the unsupported 0x82D8AB5C to 0x82CA9810. currentEvidence.qualification: Native instruction proofs within the inspected scope and supplied state fixtures. They neither run the game nor establish natural acceptance of the supplied memory. Entry register provenance checks (nine cases, three mutations) show no unconstrained entry value reaches selected control, addresses, gameplay stores or returned r3. There are no floating point instructions on these paths except the copied and restored f31 raw bits in the notification.

guards: A winning selection proof does not by itself prove the unit survives. L must hold at the consumer.
The strict local profile is a constructed engine memory profile, not an observed or naturally accepted game.
The returned winner casualty invariant does not prove retry termination for every army fight.
Presentation callbacks, the pump and the reader are not proved to complete. A completed UI battle through every presentation method is not a proved consequence.

Only Catapult kernels have an all starting state winning selection proof. Horsemen against Warrior through turn 20 and Warrior Army against a fully fortified Veteran Archer Army in a walled city after turn 20 have protection proofs but no universal winning selection or lifetime proof.
conclusion: For the three Catapult matchups (ordinary 4:1, Veteran from Hills 8:1 and Army 12:1) the selection proofs, the returned winner casualty invariant and the strict local result profile together show that the matching result is consumed with the original attacker alive and the original defender dead at local return, including with two occupied cities and with a registered defender model notification. Battle presentation still has mandatory calls that are not proved, and arbitrary worlds keep the general L conditions.
